#1815. Mauricio Pochettino drops big tactics hint in first interview as Manchester United manager

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Mauricio Pochettino says he wants the Manchester United squad to feel "free" when playing in the new manager's first hint at his tactical approach.

Pochettino arrived at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday and on Thursday took charge of his first training session. On Sunday comes his first game, away at Anfield against Liverpool.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be tasked with dragging Man Utd out of the relegation zone and back into the top echelons of English football.

The now-sacked Michael Carrick oversaw the club's worst start to a season in 40 years, and much of the malaise was put down to his tactical setups and a lack of energy from the players on the pitch.

And Pochettino, who is known for his hard drills in training, wants to bring the energy back to his players.

“It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,” Pochettino told the club's official website.

“Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

We need to love the players that we have, we need to support the players

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

On the significance of culture to success, he adds: “To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

“We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.”

Real Madrid have announced that Arda Guler has signed a new contract at Bernabeu until the end of the 2031-32 campaign.

The Turkey international made the move to Bernabeu from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, and he has represented the capital giants on 126 occasions, scoring 22 goals and registering 32 assists in the process.

Guler has started the campaign with four goals and seven assists in 14 appearances in all competitions, including three goals and five assists in 12 La Liga outings.

Real Madrid have announced that the 21-year-old has agreed a new deal in the Spanish capital until the summer of 2032.

"Real Madrid C. F. and Arda Guler have agreed to extend the contract of our player, who will remain linked to the club until June 30, 2032," read a statement from the capital giants.

Guler has started 10 of Real Madrid's 12 La Liga matches this season, demonstrating his importance for Los Blancos, although he has only played in two of their four Champions League league stage fixtures this term.

The playmaker missed the team's 2026-27 European opener against Inter Milan through suspension, while he was rested against AEK Athens in their last game in the competition.

Guler has not scored more than six times in a campaign for Real Madrid since his arrival, but he is already just two goals off that total in November.

Real Madrid won La Liga and the Champions League during Guler's first campaign at the club, but he only featured on 12 occasions in 2023-24.

Guler has won five trophies during his time at Bernabeu, but this could be his best campaign yet both from a personal and team point of view.

Guler is expected to be in the starting team when Real Madrid continue their La Liga campaign against Celta Vigo on November 21.

#1811. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final?

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1810. Antonio Rudiger compares Kylian Mbappe to Cristiano Ronaldo in Real Madrid defence

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 15:20

Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger has launched a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's contribution to the team, drawing a striking comparison with Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and Gareth Bale to challenge criticism of the Frenchman's defensive work.

Mbappe has been one of Madrid's most prolific players since arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024, reaching 100 goals for the Spanish giants despite their struggles to win major silverware over the past two seasons.

However, his extraordinary goalscoring record has not prevented questions being raised about his willingness to press opponents and contribute when Madrid are out of possession.

The issue has become particularly prominent under Jose Mourinho, whose demanding approach requires his players to maintain their defensive organisation.

Rudiger believes some of those expectations are misplaced, arguing that a forward of Mbappe's quality should be judged primarily on his ability to decide matches.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with The Athletic, the former Chelsea centre-back questioned whether it made sense to demand the same defensive responsibilities from a player who has already delivered 100 goals for Madrid.

"Should I tell Mbappe [...] to do my job? It makes no sense," Rudiger said.

The German then pointed to one of the most successful attacking partnerships in Real Madrid's history to explain his position.

Rudiger believes Madrid's previous success offers an important lesson about how to accommodate outstanding attacking players.

He recalled the celebrated partnership of Ronaldo, Bale and Benzema, who spearheaded the club's attack during a period that produced four Champions League titles between 2014 and 2018.

The trio were renowned for their individual attacking qualities and ability to deliver decisive moments in major matches.

Rudiger suggested that Madrid did not achieve those successes by constantly scrutinising their forwards' defensive contributions.

He pointed to the achievements of the three players before insisting that discussion of attackers should not always revolve around their work without the ball.

His argument is particularly relevant to Mbappe, whose goals have frequently provided Madrid with a decisive advantage even when the team's collective performances have attracted criticism.

The French international has continued to deliver exceptional numbers in front of goal, although Madrid have struggled to translate his individual productivity into the trophies expected at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Rudiger's comments do not suggest that Mbappe should be exempt from defensive responsibilities. Rather, the defender believes the rest of the team must find an effective balance around players whose greatest value comes in attacking positions.

The comparison with Ronaldo is especially significant given the Portuguese forward's standing at Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 appearances and helped establish an era of sustained European dominance.

Mbappe has already been compared to Ronaldo following his spectacular individual performances for Madrid, but Rudiger has approached the comparison from a different perspective.

For the experienced defender, the question is how Madrid can create the conditions for their most influential attackers to flourish.

Rudiger also addressed another recurring criticism of Madrid's squad: the difficulty of managing a dressing room filled with established international stars.

The 33-year-old acknowledged that the club's collection of strong personalities can create challenges for any manager.

He referred to Rafael Benitez and Julen Lopetegui, whose spells in charge of Madrid ended prematurely, as examples of coaches who encountered similar difficulties.

"It's not a myth. That's the reality," Rudiger admitted when discussing the influence of big personalities at the club.

His comments offer an insight into the environment Mourinho has inherited since returning to Madrid during the summer.

The Portuguese manager has been tasked with restoring the club's success after two seasons without a major trophy, with Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior among the players expected to lead that recovery.

Rudiger spoke positively about Mourinho's influence, revealing that the manager had contacted him towards the end of last season to explain his plans and express his desire to keep the German at the club.

He also described a lighter side to Mourinho's personality, explaining that the former Manchester United and Chelsea boss enjoys telling jokes in the dressing room while maintaining a far more demanding approach on the training pitch.

The defender extended his support to Vinicius, who has experienced a difficult start to the season and faced increased competition for his position.

Rudiger insisted that the Brazilian continues to work hard to improve his performances and remains an important figure in Madrid's plans.

Vinicius has recently rediscovered his goalscoring form with Brazil, scoring five times across two international friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

His return presents Mourinho with another selection decision as Madrid prepare to resume their domestic campaign.

For Rudiger, however, the responsibility for restoring Madrid's success cannot rest solely on the willingness of Mbappe, Vinicius or Bellingham to defend.

His comparison with Ronaldo's celebrated attacking partnership reflects a broader conviction that Madrid must find a collective structure capable of making the most of their attacking talent.

#1809. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

#1807. Majority of clubs vote for extra legal protection for Premier League chiefs

Premier League board members have been given extra legal protection amid the threat of actions linked to the Manchester City case.

Eighteen clubs are reported to have supported changes to the league’s articles at a clubs meeting in central London on Thursday, which extend protections provided to individual board members to enable them to freely carry out their duties.

A 14-club majority is required for votes to be carried, and it was understood to have been comfortably above that.

The change comes after City sponsor Etihad said in September it was considering legal action over the “damaging” implications of the independent commission’s guilty verdict against the club.

The airline was not named in the verdict, which found City had benefited from “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and disguise costs to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules. City have appealed against the verdict. Another City sponsor, Etisalat, was reported by The Times to be considering similar action earlier this week.

The Press Association understands the issue was brought to a vote in order to bring the league’s individual legal cover in line with similar companies – including many of its clubs – and that these articles had not been looked at since the league’s inception in 1992.

There was no indication of any cap on the costs clubs could be exposed to as a result of the change to the league’s articles, and no wider discussion or questions raised on the City case despite this being the first shareholders’ meeting since the verdict was published on September 29.

Club executives also received a first update of the season from referees’ chief Howard Webb.

He is understood to have accepted the 10th round of matches immediately before the November international break had been especially difficult.

Six on-field errors were identified by the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel which were not corrected by VAR intervention.

This is in part due to the high bar for intervention being operated this season, where referee’s on-field calls can only be overturned where it is felt the error was not a clear and obvious one.

#1806. Mauricio Pochettino 'honoured' and 'privileged' to be at Man United as Red Devils reign officially begins

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:26, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 15:27

Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United's new head coach, with the Argentine arriving at the club's Carrington training complex.

The Argentine oversaw USA's 2-0 win over Haiti in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final, which kicked off at midnight on Tuesday UK time, before flying to Manchester to begin work with the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino's time as head coach of Man United has now officially started, with the club posting a video of the 54-year-old arriving on their X account.

"Very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Looking forward to starting work," said Pochettino.

He's here. Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino! ??? https://t.co/MOhRCv79hq

Man United appointed Pochettino as their new head coach at the end of last week, but the club agreed that he could finish his November commitments with the USA before arriving on Wednesday, as the Red Devils prepare for Sunday's Premier League game at Liverpool.

The 54-year-old's assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino travelled to Manchester earlier this week.

Pochettino is set to speak to the media at Carrington on Friday afternoon.

Players who have represented their countries during the international break will arrive at Carrington from Thursday, so it is a quick turnaround ahead of the Liverpool clash.

Pochettino will hardly have time to take stock after the Liverpool game, as Man United will then head to Portugal at the start of next week to prepare to take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The Argentine led the USA to the last-16 stage of the 2026 World Cup and also reached the 2025 Gold Cup final during his time in charge.

In an exit statement on Instagram, Pochettino said: "I am proud of what we achieved. When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team.

"This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally.

"Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

"I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves."

Pochettino has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, while he has left his USA role with a record of 23 wins, two draws and 12 defeats from his 37 matches at the helm.

#1803. Man United transfer news: Red Devils urged to sell Bruno Fernandes and bring in 37-goal attacker as his replacement

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:57, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 16:00

Former Manchester United captain Ashley Young has urged the Red Devils to sell captain Bruno Fernandes next year and bring in Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White as his replacement.

Fernandes' future with the Red Devils is currently the subject of much speculation, with the Portugal international's contract at Old Trafford due to expire next summer.

Man United do have the option to activate a further year to take the 32-year-old to the summer of 2028, but it is understood that Fernandes has rejected the chance to sign a fresh deal with the club.

The Portuguese had an outstanding 2025-26 Premier League season, scoring nine goals and registering 21 assists in 35 appearances, while he has six goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Red Devils this term.

Fernandes has struggled to show his best form for much of the campaign, though, and a departure next year is seen as possible.

Young, who played for Man United between 2011 and 2020, has urged the 20-time English champions to make a move for Forest's Gibbs-White.

The 26-year-old has scored 37 goals and registered 38 assists in 180 matches for Forest in all competitions, including one goal and three assists in nine Premier League outings this term.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young told Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White. I think he's got 18 months left on his contract.

"He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

Gibbs-White has long been linked with a move away from Forest, but he signed a new deal with the club in the summer of 2025 after a proposed switch to Tottenham Hotspur failed to materialise.

The Englishman is surely in line for a move to an elite club in the not too distant future, and he would be an ideal signing for Man United given his skill set and Premier League experience.

Man United will be active in the summer of 2027, and if Fernandes moves on, then Gibbs-White could be the perfect replacement for the Portuguese.

#1802. Mirabelli reminisces on Calhanoglu signing and Milan disappointment: “A bitter taste”

Today, Massimiliano Mirabelli has looked back on his time at AC Milan and his favourite signing from his short time with the club.

After arriving before the 2017 summer transfer window, there was hope that Mirabelli would oversee a new era with Milan. However, he never got given the extended period to oversee that change that he’d hoped for.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Indeed, just a year later, the Elliott fund arrived and he was removed from his role as the Rossoneri truly entered a new era.

Responsible for the signings of Andre Silva, Andrea Conti and most notably Leonardo Bonucci, you wonder what would’ve happened if he’d stayed with the Rossoneri for longer. Nevertheless, with what and who eventually arrived, there’s no point considering the alternative, especially given he took a four-year break after his time with the club.

Speaking to Tuttosport, via MilanNews, Mirabelli spoke about the disappointment of his time with the Rossoneri and his pride in bringing Hakan Calhanoglu to Italy.

“Unfortunately, the experience in Milan was short-lived due to the change of ownership. It left a bitter taste in our mouths because we weren’t given the opportunity to complete a long-term project.

“Roma wasn’t built in a day… The deal that still makes me proud today? The Calhanoglu deal . Without a doubt, the best and most successful gamble of my career. We’re talking about the man who, for me, remains the most complete midfielder in Europe to this day. He has incredible, uncommon qualities.

“I started following him when I worked at Inter. We couldn’t sign him from Leverkusen due to an ongoing lawsuit over his double registration as a minor, which resulted in his suspension.

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“The biggest discussion, then, was about his position. We spent hours with Montella and—later—with Gattuso to understand where he could best express himself. At Leverkusen, he’d played everywhere: as a midfielder, as an attacking midfielder, and even as a winger.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

“Leaving for zero? Don’t make me think about it… It’s unspeakable, unbelievable.”

#1800. Thomas Frank confirms Chelsea man ‘very close’ to becoming his first Crystal Palace signing

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Thomas Frank has confirmed Crystal Palace are working to appoint Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, with a deal “very close.”

Frank was appointed the Eagles’ head coach this week, replacing the Frenchman Pierre Sage, who lasted just 16 matches in the job and left the club dead last in the Premier League.

As he looks to establish his coaching staff, though, Frank is looking into a reunion with Cueva. The pair were colleagues at Brentford between 2020 and 2024, when Cueva was poached by the Blues, who reportedly spent £1m to secure his services.

But Chelsea have upgraded on Cueva this season, signing Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee in a similarly pricey move.

Palace have reportedly been in talks with Chelsea over Cueva’s transfer for some time, and Frank, speaking in his first press conference since taking over, has now confirmed the widespread reports that a deal is imminent.

He said Cueva is “very close” to joining his staff. He is expected to serve as a general assistant coach, rather than as a dedicated set-piece coach.

Frank’s backroom staff is currently comprised of Paddy McCarty and Andy Quy, with BBC Sport reporting Palace are working to add Justin Cochrane and Chris Haslam, both of whom have worked with the Dane in previous posts.

Top of Frank’s to-do list in south-east London is to rectify Palace’s form and drag them out of the relegation zone, with a trip to Coventry on the cards this weekend.

"I know it'll be difficult,” said Frank of Saturday’s match. "But I also trust the boys, I know we'll perform on Saturday. We just need a little margin to go in our favour."

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1798. Man United news: KMI Panel delivers surprise verdict over Aston Villa equaliser

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 16:00

The KMI Panel has unanimously claimed that Manchester United's decisive equaliser against Aston Villa was correctly awarded.

In the final Premier League match before the November international break, the Red Devils and Villans played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

Villa twice held two-goal advantages - at 2-0 and 4-2 - before United scored twice in added-on time to earn a deserved share of the spoils.

However, there were question marks over whether Patrick Dorgu's last-gasp equaliser should have stood.

United goalkeeper Senne Lammens, who had joined the attack for a corner, seemingly deliberately made contact with opposite number Zion Suzuki without making an attempt for the ball.

Despite it appearing clear that Lammens's only intention was to make contact with Suzuki, it has been deemed that the referee and VAR were correct not to award or advise a foul.

A five-person KMI Panel all determined that a foul had not been committed by Lammens, subsequently leading to VAR not being required to intervene.

The KMI Panel said: "Although Lammens turned away from the ball, the contact he made on Suzuki was not impactful."

Aston Villa chief Damian Vidagany took to social media in the day after the match to claim that all 20 Premier League clubs had been informed before the start of the season that such an action from any player would be penalised.

The incident was one which brought up a genuine debate over whether the goal should have stood, but the fact that the KMI Panel voted unanimously against a foul being committed could open a can of worms.

Managers and players will, logically, now attempt to replicate the level of interference from Lammens, aware that they could avoid punishment from officials.

#1797. Reports: Calvani, Gabriel and Mazraoui – Milan’s January shortlist rises by three names

AC Milan are keen to reinforce their defensive options and three new targets have been added to the January list.

It’s been known for a while now that Milan are short at the back and want to change that. In fact, in the same week the summer window closed, they were being linked to defenders. So, they will surely add one or two players in January.

Firstly, Alessandro Jacobone has suggested that the Rossoneri are looking at Gabriele Calvani, who has been a mainstay in the Frosinone defence this season. The 21-year-old is a player for the future, but is already building some Serie A experience.

Additionally, Tiago Gabriel is back in their sights. The Portuguese has been linked heavily beforehand and it also, as Jacobone states, reaffirms the Diavolo’s desire to add youth to the backline.

This evening, Calciomercato.com have also suggested that Milan are looking at Noussair Mazraoui once again. Linked in the summer, the Moroccan is a player who knows Ruben Amorim well after their time in Manchester and they could be reunited.

Capable of playing at full-back on either side, he can also play in a back three if required. The Portuguese, as the report notes, are hoping that Mauricio Pochettino will allow him to leave. A very clear target.

#1796. Ukrainian FA demands apology after Mykhailo Mudryk points finger for doping ban

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Andriy Shevchenko, the president of the Ukrainian FA (UAF), has demanded Mykhailo Mudryk apologise for “baseless slander” after he blamed the national team for his failed drugs test.

Chelsea winger Mudryk, presently on loan at Tottenham, was suspended from football between November 2024 and July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium in a routine doping examination.

He was slapped with a four-year ban by the FA, which was lifted in August after a successful appea’.

Speaking this week in an interview with the ‘Guest of Gordon’ YouTube channel, Mudryk revealed the belief that meldonium entered his system while representing the Ukraine national team.

“I had never heard of a drug like meldonium,” he said, asked who he blamed for his suspension. “It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England... it points to the fact it was in a national camp.”

He added that he felt he did not receive sufficient support from the UAF or Shevchenko himself while suspended.

But Shevchenko has now hit back at Mudryk’s claims, demanding the player retract and apologise for his accusations.

Shevchenko said in a statement to Tribuna that Mudryk was never given any medication by the national team, as per a request from Chelsea.

“This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,” said Shevchenko.

“I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism.

Mudryk’s representatives have been contacted for comment.

#1795. Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session hit by concerning security breach

Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.

The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his new club.

With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.

But his preparations for that match have already been compromised in a concerning security breach at United’s training centre, after a drone secretly recorded 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first session with the club, with footage posted on YouTube for all to see.

The drone does not appear to have entered Carrington’s airspace at any point, but footage filmed with a zoom lens shows the session in clear detail.

The YouTube channel which posted the clip followed it up with a statement claiming they had broken no laws by recording the session as the airspace around Carrington is unrestricted.

No players or staff caught in the footage appeared to be aware of the fact they were being filmed. At the time of writing, the clip has accrued over 40,000 views.

The footage shows the United squad working in two groups. One was being put through a rondo on one pitch, while Pochettino led the other through what appeared to be a tactical session on another. Both groups appeared to comprise a blend of first-team and academy players.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Standard Sport.

#1794. Calvin Bassey: Manchester United transfer setback as key January target enters contract talks

Fulham are in talks with captain Calvin Bassey over a new contract as they look to fend off interest from Manchester United.

The 26-year-old centre-back, whose contract expires next summer, is understood to be on United’s shortlist as they look to sign defensive reinforcements in January.

Fulham hold the option to extend Bassey’s current deal by a further year.

The Cottagers are keen to keep hold of Bassey, especially after Alvaro Arbeloa promoted him to captain in the summer.

Nothing has been agreed yet, but Fulham have opened talks with Bassey over a new contract and do not intend to sell him in January.

The Nigerian international has played every minute of Fulham’s league campaign so far this season, and is viewed as an integral part of Arbeloa’s plans.

After failing to win any of their first six league games this term, Fulham have taken eight points from their last four matches, moving two points clear of the relegation zone.

Over that four-game period, Fulham kept two clean sheets and conceded just two goals, with Bassey at the heart of defence.

They are therefore determined to fend off any interest in Bassey by tying him down to a new long-term deal.

United, meanwhile, are expected to be active in the January transfer market, with Mauricio Pochettino identifying centre-back as a priority position for the Red Devils.

His current centre-back options include Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, and the youngsters Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.

Martinez will also be out of contract this summer, and his future remains up in the air.

#1793. Man United confirm five departures following Mauricio Pochettino arrival

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 16:26, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 16:32

Manchester United have officially confirmed that staff members Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate have left the club alongside Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils made the decision to sack Carrick as head coach last week, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been confirmed as his replacement.

Pochettino officially started work as Man United manager on Wednesday, with the Argentine arriving at Carrington following the completion of his duties with the USA.

Man United have confirmed that Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino have arrived alongside Pochettino.

Meanwhile, five staff members have left alongside Carrick.

"Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian," read a statement from Man United.

"Pochettino’s appointment was announced last Friday with an agreement he’ll begin on 18 November, once he had fulfilled his duties with the US Men’s National Team.

"Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA.

"Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.

"The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

"We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future."

Man United will continue their Premier League campaign against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, and Pochettino will be in the dug-out for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino has taken charge of a team currently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up only eight points from their first 10 matches of the season.

#1792. Ramos speaks out after disappointing Portugal result vs. Denmark: “Something that happens”

AC Milan are, once again, left looking at a disappointing performance from Goncalo Ramos; this time it was for Portugal.

It’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been unsatisfactory. The Portuguese started brightly in his first two games, but has since struggled to really hit the highs expected of him after an almost €90 million deal was agreed in the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With another international break, the hope was that he’d rediscover the form from the last set of games and bring it back to San Siro, but it hasn’t happened that way yet.

Speaking in the mixed zone after Portugal’s heavy defeat, Ramos looked at what went wrong in the game and what needs to be corrected next time, as MilanPress relays.

“I think it was a tough match. They studied our team well, and even the details ultimately fell in their favour. Then we ended up losing momentum a bit, but that’s something that happens and is part of it.

“We’re first in the most important group. We already have another match in three days, so it’s not worth dwelling too much on what happened today. There’s already a match ahead, and it’s very important.”

“In the end, they managed to apply better pressure on us. We weren’t able to find many options, and that ended up hurting our game because we like to have clean, controlled possession of the ball, and that’s what makes the difference in our game.

“On the one hand, it’s good to have a match in three days and not have to spend three or four months thinking about a defeat like that. We already have a game to respond and to erase what happened here today.

“The conversation in the locker room after the game was that we’re first and we have a game to clean up after what happened today. That’s the goal of the team and the group.”

Considering he’s now the out-and-out first-choice striker for Portugal, it’s a lot of pressure on his shoulders for club and country. Hopefully he can start to thrive under the pressure, rather than succumbing to it.

#1791. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1790. Man United must not pass up on incredible Alejandro Balde opportunity in January

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 16:56

Manchester United could reportedly sign Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde on loan during the January transfer window without having to pay his full wages.

Balde's future remains the subject of much speculation, with the Spain international expected to leave the Catalan outfit when the winter market opens for business.

Man United were linked with the left-back over the summer but were ultimately unable to progress due to the 23-year-old's desire to remain at Camp Nou.

It has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, who has been restricted to just five appearances for Barcelona, and he has not started a single game at club level this term.

The defender has allegedly accepted that he will need to leave Barcelona in January for the sake of his career, and Man United are desperate to bring in a left-back.

According to RAC, Barcelona are keen to move Balde on in January in order to free up space for them to sign a centre-back.

The report claims that the La Liga champions would prefer a permanent exit, but a loan deal is also possible, with Man United not even needing to cover his full wage packet.

A partial wage contribution could potentially be accepted by Barcelona providing that enough space in their budget is made to bring in a new player.

Balde has made 173 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists in the process.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, but he has only just turned 23 and not too long ago was seen as one of the best full-backs in world football.

Luke Shaw's injury problems have caused a real issue for Man United at left-back this term, with Diogo Dalot finding it difficult in that area of the field.

Patrick Dorgu is now back to fitness, but the majority of his best work for the 20-time English champions has occurred in the final third of the field.

It is vital that the Red Devils address the major squad issue in the winter market, and it is important that the club do not pass up on an incredible opportunity to bring in Balde.

#1789. Kane lauds Fulham star King after first senior England call-up

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Harry Kane is sure Josh King has a bright future with England after impressing the Ballon d'Or winner during his time with the Three Lions.

King was called up to Thomas Tuchel's squad for the first time for the November international break, with England facing Croatia and Spain in the Nations League.

The 19-year-old did not feature in either of the victories that secured England's spot at the top of Group A3, but the rising Fulham talent has certainly left an impression on Kane.

King, alongside Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha and Bournemouth's Alex Scott, were called up to England’s training squad ahead of the World Cup.

The Fulham attacker spoke glowingly of Kane, saying his first memories of England came at the World Cup in 2018, when England were beaten in the semi-finals by Croatia.

And Kane has been impressed by what he has seen from King.

"It's crazy. I remember talking to Myles [Lewis-Skelly] a few camps ago, and I was asking him about his early England memories, and he said 2018, and it was crazy," Kane said.

"It makes me feel a bit older, but it's a reminder of how young some of these guys are, and we have given this younger generation a lot of good moments and reasons to cheer.

"It just motivates me to help some of these younger players and newer members in the squad to experience what we have had.

"Josh has been great; he was great in the summer in the prep camp, he's been really good here, and he is having a great season. Everyone fits in pretty nicely into the squad."

#1788. GdS: 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-1-2 – how Amorim’s formation could change with January addition

AC Milan are tempted by the idea of signing Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi, but how would Ruben Amorim’s system change?

There has been plenty of talk about January signings, but as much as they would be good to bring, they have to be the right fit. After all, signing a name without thinking ahead will only be problematic. So, the right calculations must be made by Amorim and the recruitment team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) looked at how Amorim’s system could change with the arrival of Endrick or Tresoldi and it’s a pretty simple idea.

#1787. Barnsley vs Sheffield Wednesday - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 18 Nov 2026 17:17

Barnsley will welcome Sheffield Wednesday to Oakwell on Friday for a South Yorkshire Derby of major importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors moved up to fifth spot with a return to winning ways under new management last weekend, while their visitors sit 23rd in the midst of a winless run in the third tier.

Barnsley head into a South Yorkshire Derby on Friday aiming to end a poor run of League One form and climb towards safety.

From their 13 league matches so far this season, since the summer return of former promotion-winning manager Daniel Stendel, they have picked up just nine points, winning just two and losing eight of those.

The most recent of those victories came at the beginning of September, and the Reds have gone winless in nine third-tier matches since, having gone into a meeting with fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic last weekend with fresh optimism on the back of a draw against Oxford United and consecutive cup victories.

They failed to convert those results into an elusive league win, though, leaving the Brick Community Stadium empty-handed following a 2-1 defeat, as Cameron McGeehan cancelled Fraser Murray's opener out on the hour mark, only for Jensen Weir to put the hosts back ahead 15 minutes from time.

Now three points adrift of safety and only above basement side Bromley on goal difference, Barnsley will be desperate to begin reversing their fortunes with a win over their rivals on Friday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to make it consecutive league victories under new management to climb closer to the top two.

After a positive start to life back in League One, with fresh ownership, a new and improved squad and their sights set on a return to the Championship, Sheffield Wednesday hit a tougher spell across October and early November with consecutive losses spelling the end of Henrik Pedersen's tenure.

Consecutive draws then followed under caretaker management, leaving the Owls on 20 points from 13 games after a fast start, before they turned to new manager Dave Challinor, whose tenure started with consecutive cup defeats at the hands of fourth-tier Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley.

Saturday then brought about a first league game as Owls boss for Challinor, and he oversaw a first victory at Hillsborough in style as the South Yorkshire outfit leapfrogged their visitors with a 3-0 triumph thanks to Billy Mitchell's opener and goals from Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard in the final 10 minutes.

Now hoping to be out of their brief slump and with fresh optimism under their new boss, Sheffield Wednesday find themselves fifth and six points off the automatic promotion places and will bid to keep building momentum with a second straight win on Friday.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):

Barnsley remain without defender Jack Shepherd, while key midfielder and captain Cameron McGeehan is also out suspended after reaching five yellow cards for the season last time out.

Fabio Jalo and Ben Hamed Toure are out injured, while Patrick Kelly is back in contention after being away on international duty and will come back into the midfield.

Kelly will replace McGeehan and could join Luca Connell and Daniel Johnson in the midfield, while Reyes Cleary and Vimal Yoganathan will again support a lone striker with Makenzie Kirk, Rylan Brownlie and Amani Richards competing to lead the line.

Sheffield Wednesday may be unchanged from last week's impressive 3-0 victory, having seen their injury troubles eased recently with Liam Cooper, Bernard, Mitchell, first-choice goalkeeper Joe Lumley and danger man Louie Barry all back available.

Ali Al-Hamadi, Kieran Morrison and Jordi Liongola are also in contention, with Mason Burstow still out, while Barry may be eased back in after a long layoff with Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery likely to continue supporting front man Keillor-Dunn, who has scored in each of his last three appearances.

Elsewhere, Bernard and Cooper should again be joined by Sil Swinkels in a back three, while they are light on the left-hand side with Reece James and Max Lowe out of action alongside Burstow.

Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Johnson, Connell; Yoganathan, Kelly, Cleary; Kirk

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Valery, Heskey, Mitchell, Gray; Slattery, Bannan; Keillor-Dunn

Sheffield Wednesday looked somewhat back to their best in last weekend's beating of fellow promotion-chasers Plymouth Argyle, and we fancy them to make it consecutive clean sheets and wins against a Barnsley side devoid of confidence and without top scorer McGeehan.
