#1786. Hansi Flick finds unexpected Frenkie De Jong solution

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 17:18, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 17:29

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick may have found an unexpected way to accommodate Frenkie de Jong in his increasingly competitive squad, with the Netherlands international demonstrating his value in an unfamiliar position during the club's recent victory over Atletico Madrid.

The 29-year-old has endured another injury-disrupted year, while the arrival of Rodri has added further competition to a midfield already featuring Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo.

Yet De Jong's performance in Barcelona's 2-1 comeback victory over Atletico on November 8 offered a reminder of why Flick continues to regard him as an important member of his squad.

Introduced at half-time with Barcelona trailing, the Dutchman was surprisingly deployed at right-back rather than in his customary midfield role.

The decision helped Barcelona gain control of possession and establish a stronger presence in the opposition half, with De Jong eventually returning to central midfield following another tactical adjustment.

His influence was reflected in the statistics: he completed 65 of his 67 passes, achieving an accuracy rate of 97%, despite playing only 45 minutes.

For a player who has repeatedly faced questions about his future at the Camp Nou, it was another example of how his particular qualities can provide solutions beyond the position traditionally associated with him.

Flick's decision to introduce De Jong at right-back was particularly significant given Barcelona's difficulties in controlling the first half against Diego Simeone's side.

The German manager replaced Brian Farinas with the former Ajax midfielder, who offered a very different interpretation of the position.

Rather than remaining close to the touchline, De Jong frequently moved into central areas when Barcelona had possession, helping his teammates progress the ball through Atletico's pressure.

His ability to receive under pressure, turn away from opponents and carry possession forward allowed Barcelona to build attacks without relying exclusively on passes from their defenders.

That mobility has been one of De Jong's defining qualities throughout his career, although his contribution does not always translate into goals or assists.

According to Mundo Deportivo, he completed 22 passes in the attacking third against Atletico, more than any other Barcelona player, despite spending the entire first half on the bench.

Barcelona's overall possession increased from 58% before the interval to 68% in the second half, during which they registered 10 attempts on goal and allowed just two.

Those improvements cannot be attributed solely to De Jong, but his introduction provided a technical outlet that had been missing earlier in the contest.

Flick subsequently moved the Dutchman back into midfield after Eric Garcia entered the match, illustrating another advantage of having a player comfortable in several positions.

De Jong has previously been used as a central defender and in more advanced midfield roles, while his experience in Barcelona's build-up play makes him particularly effective when moving between the defensive and midfield lines.

The Atletico performance offered further evidence that his versatility can be valuable even when he is not an automatic starter in his preferred position.

De Jong's situation has changed considerably since the summer of 2022, when Manchester United pursued his signature under former Ajax manager Erik ten Hag.

Barcelona were prepared to consider his departure during a period of significant financial difficulties, but the midfielder remained determined to continue his career in Catalonia.

His relationship with the club has subsequently been complicated by questions over deferred wages, recurring injuries and speculation surrounding his importance to successive managers.

Nevertheless, Barcelona demonstrated their commitment to the Dutchman by extending his contract until June 2029 in October last year.

The renewal came despite his difficult injury history, which included the ankle problems that ruled him out of Euro 2024.

He suffered another major setback during the 2026 World Cup, sustaining a knee ligament injury that prevented him from featuring during the opening months of the current campaign.

De Jong eventually returned against Real Madrid on October 25 and recently reached 300 competitive appearances for Barcelona.

However, the arrival of Rodri has created an additional selection challenge for Flick.

The Spanish international offers a more natural defensive presence at the base of midfield, while Pedri remains central to Barcelona's ability to dictate possession and create opportunities.

Gavi, Bernal, Fermin and Olmo provide further alternatives, leaving Flick with considerable flexibility but difficult decisions whenever his midfielders are fit.

De Jong's capacity to operate in several roles could therefore prove particularly useful, especially when Barcelona need additional composure during the early stages of their attacking moves.

His ability to advance with the ball also offers something different from Rodri's positional discipline and Pedri's creativity between the lines.

That does not necessarily mean De Jong will become a regular right-back. His appearance against Atletico was a tactical response to the circumstances of a particular match rather than confirmation of a permanent positional change.

There is also the continuing question of his fitness.

De Jong withdrew from the Netherlands squad during the November international break after experiencing muscular discomfort, although Barcelona subsequently confirmed that the problem was not serious.

The midfielder is expected to be available for Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, providing Flick with another important option as Rodri continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.

After years in which De Jong was frequently discussed as a potential departure, his recent performances have underlined why Barcelona have been reluctant to give up on him.

His future role may depend less on securing one fixed position in Flick's midfield than on his ability to perform several functions within the same game.

#1784. Barcelona chief Deco open to making Araujo’s Liverpool loan permanent

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Barcelona sporting director Deco is open to the idea of letting Ronald Araujo join Liverpool permanently after a strong start to his loan spell at Anfield.

Araujo, a centre-back by trade, joined Liverpool on a season-long loan and has become an instant fan favourite on Merseyside with his combative displays at right-back.

The 27-year-old has made 15 appearances across all competitions, while also proving he is a threat in the final third after scoring twice and registering an assist.

It was reported that the deal includes an option to buy the Uruguay international for £47.14m (€55m), though it remains to be seen whether Liverpool are keen to activate it.

Jeremy Jacquet has impressed since joining from Rennes, with Virgil van Dijk also out of contract at the end of the 2026-27 season. Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley have returned to team training after long-term injuries.

"I am happy for him," Deco told Catalunya Radio when asked about Araujo's positive start at Anfield. "We work for Barcelona and want what's best for the club – to win, to build the best possible squad – but we are also humans, and we also want to build relationships.

"Ronald's been one of the club captains in recent years. He has had difficult moments, but also moments of great happiness, and he has been one of the leaders of this team.

"Coming back to football, things weren't going especially well for him on the pitch. He took the decision [to join Liverpool] and we respect it.

"The most important thing for us now is seeing Ronald recovered, happy, enjoying himself and in a positive place.

"If he decides to stay, Liverpool has an option to make the deal permanent. They would also have to negotiate with him – it's not just about paying the clause – but we would be happy for several reasons [if the deal goes through].

"Firstly, because the move has worked out and because Ronald is happy and is able to continue his career successfully. We want players to succeed. Also, the money would not hurt, either."

Ronald Araujo is your @StanChart Men's Player of the Month for October https://t.co/WqIsWeFGJv

Araujo's move was reportedly seen as a one-off by Liverpool, who were short in defence ahead of Andoni Iraola's first season in charge.

He was restricted to 16 starts in all competitions last season, having only made 17 in 2024-25. In each of Barcelona's previous three campaigns, Araujo started at least 30 games.

The defender was also granted a mental health break of just over a month midway through 2025-26, but he has wasted little time in settling into the Premier League.

In the top flight this season, only Jacquet (68) has won more duels than Araujo's 49, while he also ranks second for aerial duels won (30) and clearances (40) in Liverpool's ranks.

Deco confirmed there is a deadline for Liverpool to decide if they are willing to pay the fee to bring in Araujo, though he said exceptions could be made to strike a deal.

"In football, you can always negotiate," Deco added. "There is a deadline for exercising the option, just as there is when we bring players in on loan.

"After that, you can always try to negotiate and work things out. It will depend on the circumstances at the time, on us, on the player and on various other factors."

#1783. Klopp breaks ranks to savage Infantino: Liverpool legend becomes first boss to turn on FIFA president - who is WORSE than Sepp Blatter - as pressure mounts after World Cup farce

Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026

Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so

The Germany manager said Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager said.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion plan fell apart.

But he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his plan. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE company.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

In terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

After his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime shows.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment company, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the company take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

#1779. Trafford’s England heroics come as no surprise to Leeds boss Farke

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Daniel Farke admitted he was surprised that everyone was so shocked by James Trafford's display during England's thrilling Nations League win over Spain.

Trafford was selected to start ahead of the Three Lions' final Group A3 fixture against the reigning world champions, and he more than played his part in their 3-2 victory.

England were three goals ahead thanks to strikes from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White before Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal.

Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams were able to find a way past the Leeds goalkeeper, but in the latter stages at the Metropolitano, Trafford produced a string of important stops, including a superb double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte.

But Trafford's display did not come as a shock to Farke, whose Leeds side have conceded just eight Premier League goals so far this season.

Only Arsenal (five) and Brighton (seven) have let in fewer, while Trafford has made the second-most saves (37) and has the best save ratio (81.4%) in the competition in 2026-27.

"I'm a bit bored because in my last 237 press conferences I've been praising him and right now the whole country is praising him," Farke said of Trafford.

"I'm surprised that everyone is so surprised that our goalkeeper is capable of delivering a top performance. That is why he wears the gloves.

"I also expect him to catch some balls and make some saves. I'm not surprised he's had a good performance."

Trafford will expect to busy again this weekend when Leeds make the trip to Stamford Bridge to face a Chelsea side who signed off for the international break with a defeat.

Enzo Le Fee's first-half penalty was enough to earn Sunderland a 1-0 win, a result that saw Xabi Alonso's side drop out of the top four at the expense of Liverpool.

Valentin Barco was an unused substitute at the Stadium of Light and was unable to see any minutes for Argentina in their defeat to Uruguay and 7-0 thrashing of Costa Rica.

Barco has only made four Premier League appearances for Chelsea this season, totalling 119 minutes, but he believes he will eventually come good at Stamford Bridge.

"As a player, you always want to play so you are not happy when you don't, but I understand this is the best national team in the world," Barco told ESPN.

"But I'm happy to come to the national team, to continue to represent my country. I will now try to play at Chelsea and contribute."

"I think I can give a lot more. I also said the same thing when I was at Strasbourg; even when I was playing well, I knew I could give more because I know what I can give.

"I have a lot of confidence in myself, so I have to keep working to continue growing."

Only Joao Pedro (eight) has more goal involvements than Rogers in the Premier League for Chelsea this season (six – five goals, one assist), but after an encouraging international break with England, he will be full of confidence.

Rogers also boasts a good record against Leeds in the top-flight. Only against Manchester United and Bournemouth (both three) has he netted more times against than Leeds (two, level with four other teams).

Of the players to play 500+ minutes since the start of February, only Benjamin Sesko (one every 83 minutes) has a better minutes-per-goal ratio in the Premier League than Okafor, who has netted eight goals in 894 minutes of action (one every 112 minutes).

He has also now scored eight goals across his last 16 Premier League appearances, having netted just two in his first 21 in the competition.

Beautiful scenes! https://t.co/GYpuRXqBZi

Chelsea have won eight of their last 10 home games against Leeds in all competitions (D2) since a 2-0 loss in December 1999. They have already beaten the Whites 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in the EFL Cup this season.

The Blues have also won 10 points from five top-flight home games this season (W3 D1 L1), their most after five home matches since 2022-23 under Thomas Tuchel/Graham Potter (11), and their most at the start of a campaign under a new manager since 2018-19 under Maurizio Sarri (11).

But this could be an intriguing battle at both ends of the pitch. Leeds have generated the most expected goals (xG) from set-pieces (excl. penalties) in the Premier League this season (6.1), with their only two goals across their last four league games coming from a throw-in and a corner.

Chelsea, meanwhile, have conceded the second-most goals from set-pieces (eight) in the big five European leagues in 2026-27 (Monza – nine, excluding penalties).

Leeds avoided defeat in both Premier League meetings with Chelsea last season (3-1 home, 2-2 away), last going unbeaten in three in a row against the Blues between November 2000 and October 2001.

However, Leeds have won just one of their last 25 matches in London in all competitions (D6 L18), a 3-0 win at Millwall in September 2023. Four of their last five defeats have come in the capital, including two against Chelsea: 1-0 at Wembley in the FA Cup in April and 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in September.

#1778. Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432

Given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil said: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” said Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is important], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a big game in keeping that momentum.”

"We said at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not.  Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

The game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur

The teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm)

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the new season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

#1777. Real Madrid: Vini Jr "hasn't been the same" since this one star name left

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 17:46

Vinicius Junior's struggles at Real Madrid have as much to do with the departure of Toni Kroos as the arrival of Kylian Mbappe, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

The Brazilian ended 2026 on a high for his country, scoring twice in Saturday's 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan before hitting a first-half hat-trick in Tuesday's 7-0 rout of Singapore, his first treble for the Selecao.

Those five goals offered a stark contrast to his club form; Vinicius managed just one goal for Real Madrid before the first international break of 2026-27, and he was then handed a four-match La Liga ban for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba, ruling him out of El Clasico.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery suggested that restoring the forward's confidence had been one of Carlo Ancelotti's main objectives for the window, while pointing to an issue that has received little attention.

"From the moment Mbappe was signed by Real Madrid, how do you fit the two of them together, both in tactical and temperamental terms?" Vickery said.

"Vini had been the main man. He'd won them Champions Leagues. Mbappe comes in and he's almost promoted above him as the star turn.

"They both like to retreat and attack from that space wide on the left. That was always going to be difficult, and it has proved difficult.

"But there's one thing that is possibly even more important, and I haven't seen many people talk about it: the loss of Toni Kroos. I think it's no coincidence that Vini hasn't been the same player since."

Kroos retired after Euro 2024, the same summer in which Mbappe arrived from Paris Saint-Germain, and Vickery believes the absence of a midfield conductor is now hurting Vinicius for both club and country.

"You can't really win the game down the flanks without having some kind of control in the centre of midfield," he added.

"That's been Ancelotti's problem with Brazil so far as he tries to get the best out of Vini, and I think that's Vini's problem with Real Madrid as well.

"He was so much a better player when he had the passing range of Toni Kroos as his supply line. I don't know how Real Madrid are going to solve that one."

Vinicius will now return to Jose Mourinho's side ahead of Saturday's La Liga meeting with Celta Vigo, hoping his international goal spree can spark a revival. However, Vickery's assessment suggests a lasting solution may depend on Real Madrid's recruitment in the centre of the park, rather than on the Brazilian alone.

#1772. Mauricio Pochettino's first words at Tottenham, PSG, Chelsea and USA reveal Man United approach

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40

Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.

The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United sit 18th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 10 matches, with Michael Carrick's dismissal leaving Pochettino responsible for restoring confidence to a squad struggling for results.

The 54-year-old has inherited troubled teams before, although few appointments have offered such little preparation time before a fixture of this magnitude.

Looking back at his opening statements in four previous jobs reveals a recurring approach: Pochettino tends to publicly back the players he inherits, avoid making immediate transfer demands and emphasise the importance of collective responsibility.

Those principles have helped him transform some teams, but his experiences at PSG and Chelsea also demonstrate that they do not guarantee success.

When Pochettino arrived at Tottenham in 2014, the club were searching for stability after a disappointing campaign under Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood.

The Argentine had built his reputation at Southampton, where his energetic pressing system and ability to develop young players attracted considerable attention.

At his first major press engagement with Spurs, he resisted suggestions that widespread recruitment was necessary.

"We have an unbelievable squad with unbelievable players," Pochettino insisted.

"The most important thing is to develop our players and to provide the best team to play on the pitch."

His message was clear: improving the existing squad would take priority over demanding new signings.

That approach eventually helped Tottenham establish themselves among the Premier League's leading clubs.

Pochettino guided Spurs to second place in 2016-17 and reached the Champions League final in 2019, although he departed later that year without winning a trophy.

His appointment at PSG in January 2021 presented a different challenge.

Rather than developing a relatively young Premier League squad, Pochettino inherited a team containing established superstars, including Neymar and Kylian Mbappe.

During his introductory press conference, the Argentine again rejected the idea of imposing a rigid tactical system regardless of the available personnel.

Discussing the roles of Neymar and Mbappe, he explained that his responsibility was to find positions in which they could express their abilities and become decisive.

He also emphasised that a team's behaviour with and without possession mattered more than the formation displayed on paper.

The flexibility he promised was tested by the demands of managing an exceptionally talented squad.

Although PSG won Ligue 1 in 2021-22, Pochettino failed to deliver the Champions League success the club wanted and departed that summer.

Chelsea offered another rebuilding assignment in 2023.

The Blues had finished 12th in the Premier League after a turbulent campaign, and Pochettino was tasked with restoring their competitiveness following extensive changes to the playing squad.

At his first press conference, he acknowledged that performances alone would not satisfy expectations at Stamford Bridge.

The Argentine also expressed confidence in the club's sporting structure, explaining that he had accepted the owners' strategic plan rather than seeking greater authority over recruitment.

His Chelsea side eventually recovered to finish sixth and reached the EFL Cup final, but an inconsistent campaign ended with his departure by mutual consent in May 2024.

The experience demonstrated the difficulty of introducing a long-term playing philosophy while facing pressure for immediate results.

Pochettino's introductory press conference with the United States in September 2024 provided perhaps the clearest indication of the demands United's players can expect.

The former Tottenham manager made collective effort central to his philosophy, insisting that individual talent would only be effective within a properly organised team.

"But when we don't have the ball, we need to run, we need to be aggressive, we need to be competitive," he explained.

He also stressed that his coaching staff needed to create an environment in which players understood their responsibilities and could express their abilities.

That message carries particular relevance at Old Trafford.

United have conceded 19 goals in their opening 10 Premier League matches and have struggled to produce the collective intensity required to compete consistently.

Pochettino's preference for coordinated pressing could offer one route towards improvement, although implementing those principles will require time and careful management of the squad's physical condition.

His previous appointments suggest that he is unlikely to begin by publicly criticising individual players or demanding a major January overhaul.

At Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea, his introductory message focused on working with the players already available, with recruitment generally left to the club's decision-makers.

That approach may be particularly important at United, where the relationship between the head coach and the sporting department will come under scrutiny as the January transfer window approaches.

Pochettino also has a record of improving young players, an asset for a squad featuring talents such as Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo and Benjamin Sesko.

However, the circumstances surrounding his arrival leave little opportunity for a gradual introduction.

Unlike at Chelsea, where he benefited from a full pre-season, the Argentine has only a handful of training sessions before facing Liverpool.

United's position in the relegation zone also creates a more urgent challenge than the long-term projects he initially discussed at Tottenham or with the United States.

His opening press conferences across those four jobs suggest he will seek to protect his players publicly while demanding greater effort and discipline behind the scenes.

Whether those familiar principles can produce an immediate response will become clearer at Anfield, where Pochettino faces one of the most difficult possible introductions to life as Manchester United manager.

#1771. ‘I tried everything’ to convince Guimaraes to stay at Newcastle, says Jaissle

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Matthias Jaissle conceded Bruno Guimaraes' mind was already made up on joining Arsenal despite trying his hardest to keep the Brazilian at Newcastle United.

Guimaraes is set to return to St. James' Park for the first time since completing his reported £75m transfer to the Premier League champions in the summer.

He joined Newcastle from Lyon in 2022 and went on to make 195 appearances across all competitions, scoring 31 goals and providing 31 assists for the Magpies.

The 29-year-old also captained Newcastle to their first domestic trophy in 70 years in the EFL Cup last March, but he made his intentions clear of an exit after last season.

Since joining Arsenal, Guimaraes has played 14 times across all competitions and scored two goals, one of which came against Newcastle's rivals Sunderland.

"I met him shortly in pre-season, but his decision was already made to join Arsenal," Jaissle said when asked about the missed opportunity of working with Guimaraes.

"I tried my best, but the decision was made, so now we are opponents and competitors. Our approach is to give not only him, but also his team-mates, a difficult 90 minutes.

"I just said that we counted on him as a leader last year. I tried to explain the role he would've had with us, but again the decision was already made before I even spoke with him.

"I felt it was my job to do my best anyway, at least then I can look in the mirror and say: 'I tried everything'."

When asked about the reception Guimaraes should receive on his return to St. James' Park, Jaissle said: "That's not something I should influence. I don't have thoughts on that."

Back to business at St. James' Park on Saturday! https://t.co/VDGwD9Jx7c

— Newcastle United (@NUFC) November 18, 2026

Newcastle signed off for the international break with a 1-1 draw away to Fulham, a result that leaves them 12th in the table after 10 games of the season.

The Magpies have won just one of their last 29 Premier League games against sides starting the day top of the table (D8 L20), and none of their last 18 (D4 L14) since a 2-1 victory over Chelsea in December 2014.

Newcastle are also winless in 14 Premier League games against reigning champions (D5 L9) since beating Manchester City 2-1 in January 2019.

And their struggles this year have surprisingly come at home. No side has lost more Premier League home games in 2026 than Newcastle (seven), who have lost both of their last two at St. James' Park without scoring.

Not since February 2014 have they lost more in a row without a goal at home in the competition (run of four), but Jaissle believes the Newcastle fans could be key to beating Mikel Arteta's side.

"If you face the champions, that is motivation enough," Jaissle added. "We are playing at home in front of our fans; they can be the twelfth man.

"The fans can give us so much power and support. This is a great opportunity, a big challenge."

#1770. Nottingham Forest: 21-year-old transfer target could be "eaten up" in Premier League

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 20:30

Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

The Santos midfielder has reportedly been tracked by Forest for much of 2026, with Oliver Glasner's side weighing up a move in the January transfer window. Bournemouth are also said to be interested.

Bontempo, who turns 22 in January, has enjoyed a breakthrough year, contributing six goals and five assists in 50 appearances, and he earned his first Brazil call-up in September.

The lynchpin's contract runs until 2030, though, and speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery expressed doubts over whether the youngster could handle the step up to English football.

"He's had to grow up very quickly as a central midfielder with Santos," Vickery said. "His first year was a prolonged battle against relegation, and it is a team full of veterans, which puts a lot of strain on a young midfielder.

"He really has to cover the ground and link the play. He's a good little give-and-go midfielder.

"Premier League, now I have my doubts. He's around the six-foot mark, so he's not small, but he is physically quite flimsy.

"Everyone who comes from South American football to the Premier League says the same thing: 'You've got to play quicker. You must know what you're going to do with the ball before it comes.'

"In a Premier League midfield, I think he could be eaten up. I wouldn't see him as a player who's Premier League ready at the moment."

Rather than Bontempo, Vickery believes Forest should consider a familiar face in Danilo.

The 25-year-old broke his ankle on the opening day of the 2024-25 season against Bournemouth, and he joined Botafogo the following summer in a club-record deal worth around €22m (£19.2m).

Danilo was in superb form during the first half of 2026 and earned a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, but his hopes of securing a move to a Premier League side playing in the Champions League have yet to materialise.

"Forest could do a lot worse than get the left-footed, strong, quick-thinking, versatile Danilo back," Vickery added.

"At the moment, he's a better bet than Gabriel Bontempo, who is certainly one for the long term rather than now."

Danilo scored six goals and set up four more in 10 appearances for Nottingham Forest and was also linked with Manchester United during the summer transfer window.

Published: 06:21 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 16 November 2026

Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.

England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.

Thomas Tuchel’s side were three goals in front and cruising when Anderson - looking to atone for a sloppy error from Jarrel Quansah - cynically hauled down 19-year-old Yamal as he barrelled down on goal.

Spain were awarded a penalty for the infringement, and Anderson was sent off - much to the Manchester City star’s bemusement.

But Yamal, aggrieved by Anderson’s challenge, made a beeline for the midfielder following the challenge. According to Spanish reports, the attacker mouthed ‘tonto, tonto’ to his rival following his dismissal.

The colloquial term can mean a number of things, varying from idiot, fool or stupid, but in any case is far from a term of affection.

A fired-up Yamal galvanised the reigning world champions as they searched for an unlikely comeback.

Mikel Oyarzabal, the man who scored Spain’s winner against England two years ago in the 2024 Euros final, converted the spot kick before Nico Williams scored Spain’s second after latching on to an excellent Yamal cross.

However, Las Rojas fell short, with Sunday’s defeat their first in an imperious 43-game run.

A jubilant Thomas Tuchel hailed the match as his ‘best performance of my time as manager’.

‘It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.’

Nico Paz is reportedly set to spark a tussle for his signature after Mauricio Pochettino's recent appointment at Manchester United.

United also reportedly face fierce competition from across the continent, with Premier League rivals Arsenal and Chelsea alongside Paris Saint-Germain all closely monitoring his rapid progression.

The source above believes that Pochettino should receive substantial financial backing from the club hierarchy when the winter transfer window opens in January.

The need for defensive reinforcements has grown increasingly urgent amid reports that Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez wants out of Old Trafford despite earning plaudits for his recent international displays.

#1766. Lampard: Decisions went against Coventry in defeat to Everton

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Frank Lampard was still left questioning the decisions made during Coventry City's 3-1 defeat to Everton as they prepare to bounce back against Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Coventry signed off for the international break with a loss at Hill Dickinson Stadium, despite taking the lead through Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute strike past Jordan Pickford.

However, Thierno Barry led Everton's fightback with two goals before teeing up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, though Lampard expressed his confusion about some of the decisions.

And on Wednesday, the independent Key Match Incidents panel concluded that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski fouled Caleb Yirenkyi.

There was also wide-scale debate over Thierno Barry's second goal and whether it was handball, with the Everton forward squeezing the ball in at Carl Rushworth's near post.

"It's a game we lost because of decisions, in my opinion," Lampard told reporters of those findings. "There were decisions that went wrongly against us by the referee.

"I appreciate they were honest after the event, but that doesn't help us. Going away from home is not easy, but I felt like we deserved a result. We must keep going.

"These things happen in football so we have to keep positive and keep going."

Thank you for your support on the road this evening, safe travels home. https://t.co/FFMkr8xTAh

— Coventry City (@CoventryCityFC) November 6, 2026

There will be a new face in the Palace dugout at the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend, with Thomas Frank set to take charge of his first game with the Eagles.

Frank was appointed as Palace's new boss following the sacking of Pierre Sage, who left the club sitting bottom of the Premier League after 10 matches.

Only two of Palace's 13 previous permanent managers in the Premier League have won their first game in charge (D4 L7 – first spells only), with Alan Pardew beating Tottenham in January 2015 and Oliver Glasner beating Burnley in February 2024.

And when asked about his hopes for the rest of the season, Frank outlined his ambition to help Palace compete on all fronts, including the EFL Cup and Europa League.

"Of course, I've looked at the team and done a lot of analysis on the team. I think there's a lot of positives, definitely," Frank said.

"There's no doubt, to state the obvious, that we need to stabilise things. That's one thing. We need to work incredibly hard.

"Obviously, we're conceding too many goals that we need to address, so we need to work on the defensive side of things with principles, attitude, everything regarding that.

"Then, of course, it's one game at a time. We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe. There are two fantastic cup tournaments, but, of course, the Premier League is the most important, if we need to prioritise. But we would like to compete on all fronts."

Rudoni is one of six players who are both their team's leading shot taker (17) and chance creator (17) in the top-flight this season, alongside Chelsea's Cole Palmer, Palace's Yeremy Pino, Ipswich Town's Julio Enciso, Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes, and Newcastle United's Harvey Barnes.

He is also the only Coventry City player to score more than once in the Premier League this season (three).

Despite falling to a 3-1 defeat against Liverpool ahead of the international break, one positive for Palace was to see Nketiah get himself on the scoresheet.

Nketiah scored his first goal in the Premier League this season, netting for the first time since December 2025 against Fulham, and with Jean-Philippe Mateta still serving a suspension, Frank could give him the nod up front ahead of Jorgen Strand Larsen.

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 16, 2026

This is the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal in any competition since March 2012, a 1-1 draw in the Championship.

Coventry have lost just one of their six Premier League games against Palace (W2 D3), with this the first meeting since a 3-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 1998.

The Sky Blues have, however, lost seven or more of their opening 10 games of a league campaign for only the third time ever, also doing so in their first two Football League seasons in 1919-20 (nine) and 1920-21 (seven). It is already as many defeats as they suffered in last season's Championship.

But they face a Palace side that have conceded 24 goals in 10 Premier League games this season, their most at this stage of a season since 1980-81 under Terry Venables (also 24).

Indeed, 10 of the 15 sides to have conceded that many goals in their first 10 Premier League games have been relegated, though Wolves did it most recently in 2024-25 (27 conceded) and ended the season in 16th.

Palace won their first four visits to the Coventry Building Society Arena between 2005 and 2008 but are winless in their last four in all competitions between 2009 and 2012 (D2 L2), making Frank's debut all the more tricky.

#1765. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”
